title: dedicated-gpu-pool-scheduling-autoscale-warmup-debug-breadcrumbs-3
content:
Summary:
- Short: Dedicated GPU pool experienced repeated capacity thrash during batch inference spikes. Autoscaler oscillated: scaled up new nodes, nodes became Ready slowly (GPU driver + device-plugin warm), scheduler kept queuing pods -> autoscaler scaled up again -> later scaled down, causing request latency spikes and throttling.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-02-20 14:05 UTC: spike in batch traffic (redwood-hosted ingest) -> queued pods start appearing (Pending).
- 14:06 UTC: autoscaler triggered +4 nodes (g4dn-like instances) to satisfy pending pods.
- 14:08 UTC: nodes appear as NotReady for ~90-180s; device-plugin logs show "registration delayed".
- 14:09-14:15 UTC: scheduler still reports many pods Pending; autoscaler triggers another +3 nodes.
- 14:20 UTC: first nodes become Ready; pods start scheduling and then ContainerCreating hangs due to driver init time (nvidia-container-cli timeouts).
- 14:30 UTC: traffic drops; autoscaler scales down nodes aggressively; residual pods get rescheduled, causing further churn.

Commands / queries I ran: (copied-output style)
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide
  -> showed ~120 pending pods across default/serving namespaces, many with nodeSelector: "dedicated-gpu=true"
- kubectl describe pod <pending-pod>
  -> Events: 0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu OR node(s) had taint that the pod didn't tolerate
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  -> new nodes show "NotReady" for ~2-3 minutes, with unschedulable=false while NotReady
- kubectl logs daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin -n kube-system -l app=nvidia-device-plugin --tail=200
  -> repeated: "device plugin: failed to register: timeout waiting for /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins" and intermittent "driver not ready"
- kubectl logs -n kube-system kubelet-<node> (grep nvidia)
  -> "nvidia-container-cli: could not select device: device initialization timed out"
- Prometheus: sum(pending_pods{pool="dedicated-gpu"}) over 5m -> spike from 5 -> 120 in 2min
- Prometheus: rate(kube_node_status_condition{condition="Ready",status="false"}[1m]) -> small spike correlating with scale-up
- grafana: per-node GPU-utilization graph shows near-0 until ~5-10m after node becomes Ready

Log / error snippets copied: 
- "Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal   NotTriggerScaleUp  2m    cluster-autoscaler  Skipped: node has taint dedicated-gpu:NoSchedule
  Warning  FailedScheduling  30s   default-scheduler    0/10 nodes are available: Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu"

- device-plugin: "time="2026-02-20T14:07:10Z" level=error msg="failed to get device list: driver not responding""
- kubelet: "E0214 14:08:32.123] nvidia-container-cli: device initialization timed out"

Observed signals / metrics: 
- Rapid growth in pending pods for pool selector dedicated-gpu=true.
- ClusterAutoscaler added nodes in batches; scale-up latency ~1.5-3m.
- Node Ready -> GPU plugin init -> driver init -> node effectively usable: additional ~3-6m before pods reach Running and GPU-util shows >0.
- Autoscaler scale-down policy uses underutilized CPU-based metric (node CPU < 20% for 5m) which was true because pods were Pending and not consuming CPU -> premature scale-down.
- Node taints/labels: some nodes created with label gpu-type=v100 while pods expected gpu-type=A100 (mismatch observed in one set).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Warmup/driver-init latency is the dominant factor. Autoscaler expects nodes to be usable within ~2m; actual GPU readiness takes 5–10m because of driver install/warm steps and device-plugin delays. This leads to repeated scale-ups.
2) Scale-down policy is too aggressive and keyed on CPU/Memory not GPU-ready signal. Idle nodes get removed before they serve queued pods.
3) Taints/tolerations or nodeLabel mismatches cause scheduler to skip newly launched nodes (some nodes created with different label set), so autoscaler keeps adding more nodes.
4) Device-plugin intermittently fails to register (maybe due to kernel/nvidia-driver mismatch or image with older cuda toolchain).
5) Pre-provisioned warm pool not sufficient at this traffic level (we need a small always-on buffer).

Actions tried so far (what changed / what rolled back):
- Increased cluster-autoscaler scale-up batch limit from 5 -> 8 temporarily (no real improvement, just larger spikes).
- Turned off aggressive scale-down: changed scale-down-unneeded-time from 5m -> 15m for one test cluster (reduced churn but costier).
- Added Pod toleration for dedicated-gpu:NoSchedule on a few test pods to force scheduling (revealed driver init errors).
- Deployed a pre-warm DaemonSet that runs a lightweight GPU probe container on new nodes (helped identify driver init timing but didn't fix timeouts).
- Locked a subset of pool nodes to use the same gpu-type label as pods (gpu-type=A100) — fixed label mismatch for that subset, saw scheduling improve for pods matching that label.
- Opened INFRA JIRA INFRA-2345 to track device-plugin timeouts and driver version skew (assigned to infra-driver team).

Short-term mitigations recommended: (order by impact)
- Increase scale-down grace window to 15m for dedicated GPU pool (reduce thrash).
- Change autoscaler scale decision to consider "pending_pods_for_pool > 0" and only scale down when pending_pods==0 for a period.
- Prewarm a small always-on buffer of nodes (2-4 nodes depending on pool size) with correct labels and drivers.
- Add a "gpu-ready" custom metric exported by node-exporter (true when device-plugin registered and nvidia-smi returns OK) and use it in scale decisions.

Longer-term fixes to evaluate: 
- Bake GPU drivers + device-plugin into node image (reduce init time to < 30s).
- Use instance start hooks to signal when GPU kernel modules + driver are ready (node condition).
- Change scale-down to consider node annotation "gpu-allocated=true" and pending pod count across pool.
- Consider predictive autoscaling (use recent traffic patterns to pre-scale by a small delta).
- Evaluate warm-pool implementation (keep warm instances in stopped/standby state to reduce start time).

Reproduction steps (dev cluster):
1) Set up dedicated-gpu pool autoscaler with current prod config (scale-up delay=2m, scale-down-unneeded-time=5m, bucket-size=5).
2) Create a job that submits 200 short-lived pods with nodeSelector: dedicated-gpu=true over 30s.
3) Observe pending_pods metric, cluster-autoscaler events, node Ready times, device-plugin logs.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- Why does device-plugin occasionally fail to register on newly created nodes? Kernel mismatch or timing? Need node init logs and package versions (rpm/dpkg list) collected at boot.
- Are we using a node image that installs drivers on first boot (apt) or baked AMI? If apt-based, network slowness may exacerbate warmup.
- Can we add a node condition (like "GPUReady") from kubelet to make autoscaler decisions easier?

Useful artifacts to attach / next steps for handoff:
- Collect full kubelet logs + dmesg from sample NotReady node (attach to INFRA-2345).
- Export prometheus queries used: pending_pods_for_pool = sum(kube_pod_status_phase{phase=Pending, label_pool="dedicated-gpu"})
- Run a controlled repro on staging with variable prewarm sizes (0,2,4) and capture: scale-up count and time to first Running pod.
- Follow up with infra-driver team: confirm node AMI build (baked drivers) or bootstrap path.

Notes / misc: 
- Saw one instance where pod spec used nodeSelector gpu-type=A100 but autoscaler created nodes labeled gpu-type=v100 (config mismatch between pool config and instance template). Look into Terraform module that assembles node labels.
- For short-term incident response, I set scale-down-unneeded-time=20m and added 3 prewarm nodes -> incident did not reoccur during next traffic spike (cost spike acceptable for short window).

Contact: Jordan Patel (eng-serving-runtime) - ping in #infra-gpu-autoscale or DM for logs/hand-off.

Attachments (I will paste links into the Jira):
- grafana snapshot: (placeholder) https://grafana.redwood/s/gw123/pending-pods-spike
- prom query: sum(kube_pod_status_phase{phase=Pending, label_pool="dedicated-gpu"}) by (namespace)
- infra ticket: INFRA-2345

-- end of notes --
